summary: Not accepted. The source fingerprint, 113-command passing report and both retained compiler archives are consistent, but release delivery has an incompatible review-path guard, phase completion omits delivery verification, and the packaged example introduces a Windows compilation regression.

findings.description: The registry-readiness guard accepts only phase-31-attempt-NN.json, while phase 31 requires phase-31-chunk-release-readiness-codex-attempt-NN.json. I reproduced rejection of the required Codex path. Consequently, the documented delivery verifier cannot accept a valid 0.2.5 registry receipt.
findings.required_fix: Select the correct Codex chunk filename format for phase 31 while preserving historical formats. Add a regression covering registry-readiness verification with an accepted phase-31 Codex record.

findings.description: Complete-phase acceptance checks chunk reviews and immediately marks phase 31 complete without invoking release_delivery.verify. The phase-31 command set also omits that verifier. Missing, stale or subsequently altered registry/tag/CI receipts therefore cannot prevent completion once reviews pass, unlike the existing release advancement path in review_phase.py.
findings.required_fix: Require successful current-source phase-31 delivery verification before recording completion. Add tests proving missing, stale and failed delivery evidence blocks advancement despite accepted reviews.

findings.description: The new std::os::unix imports and permission methods are unconditional within a feature-gated module. Windows builds with gateway and reqwest-transport enabled cannot compile this packaged example, including the configured Windows native all-feature workflow.
findings.required_fix: Conditionally compile Unix permission handling and provide a secure non-Unix implementation or an explicit unsupported-platform fallback. Verify Windows example compilation without weakening private-file protections.

evidence: Read AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/PHASES.md, the accepted Portkey plan and phase-31 status.
Independently recomputed fingerprint 8be0f8a5e75f100a42b57c5f9de330c3be7d8923ec9cfbfdd738f95725fc3bef; all 113 recorded commands exactly match commands_for(31), with zero exits and no timeouts.

Inspected both schema-3 package receipts and retained archives: archive hashes, sizes, member inventories and source/example bytes match; recorded extracted-package checks passed on Rust 1.89.0 and 1.99.0.
Inspected release scripts, review gates, related regression tests, workflow configuration, documentation and ledger changes against phase 30.
Executed a read-only reproduction of the phase-31 registry-readiness filename rejection.
Executed both offline live-receipt validators successfully. MCP evidence records 19 successful steps and complete cleanup; general live evidence verifies one native method.
limitations: Did not rerun compiler, package or full test suites; inspected their recorded execution evidence and independently checked archive integrity.
Windows compilation failure is established by source inspection, not a Windows compiler run.
No network requests, tenant access, credential reads or checkout modifications occurred.
Remote publication, annotated tags, terminal CI and Docusaurus delivery remain pending later chunks; their absence alone was not treated as a readiness finding.
